content: The drug rifampin interacts with various medications by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4, which can significantly alter the metabolism and effectiveness of these drugs. Below is a detailed explanation of these interactions: 1. Enzalutamide: Rifampin reduces enzalutamide levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, increase the enzalutamide dose from 160 mg daily to 240 mg daily. Upon discontinuation of rifampin, revert to the original enzalutamide dose. 2. Erdafitinib: Rifampin decreases erdafitinib levels by altering its metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, separate administration by at least 6 hours to minimize interaction. 3. Ergotamine: Rifampin reduces ergotamine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Erlotinib: Rifampin decreases erlotinib levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Erythromycin (all forms): Rifampin reduces erythromycin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Estradiol and other estrogens: Rifampin decreases estradiol and other estrogen levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Use non-hormonal contraceptives as an alternative. 7. Etonogestrel: Rifampin reduces etonogestrel levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Etrasimod: Rifampin decreases etrasimod levels by inducing CYP3A4, CYP2C8, and CYP2C9 enzymes. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 9. Everolimus: Rifampin reduces everolimus levels through CYP3A4 induction and P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporter effects. Co-administration is contraindicated. 10. Fedratinib: Rifampin decreases fedratinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Felbamate: Rifampin reduces felbamate levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Felodipine: Rifampin decreases felodipine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 13. Fesoterodine: Rifampin reduces fesoterodine levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Fexinidazole: Rifampin increases fexinidazole levels by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Fineranone: Rifampin decreases fineranone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Fludrocortisone: Rifampin reduces fludrocortisone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Fosamprenavir: Rifampin decreases fosamprenavir levels through CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 18. Fosaprepitant: Rifampin reduces fosaprepitant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 19. Fostamatinib: Rifampin decreases fostamatinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Fruquintinib: Rifampin reduces fruquintinib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Futibatinib: Rifampin decreases futibatinib levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Ganaxolone: Rifampin reduces ganaxolone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers. If unavoidable, consider increasing the ganaxolone dose without exceeding the maximum daily dose. 23. Gepirone: Rifampin decreases gepirone levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Gilteritinib: Rifampin reduces gilteritinib levels by affecting P-gp and CYP3A4 substrates. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Glasdegib: Rifampin decreases glasdegib levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir: Rifampin reduces glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels via CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 27. Hydrocortisone: Rifampin decreases hydrocortisone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Hydroxyprogesterone Caproate: Rifampin reduces hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 29. Ibrutinib: Rifampin decreases ibrutinib levels significantly (~10-fold) by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 30. Idelalisib: Rifampin reduces idelalisib levels through CYP3A4 induction. 31. Iloperidone: Rifampin decreases iloperidone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Indinavir: Rifampin reduces indinavir levels by increasing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. 33. Infigratinib: Rifampin decreases infigratinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Irinotecan (and liposomal form): Rifampin reduces irinotecan levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Isoniazid: Rifampin increases isoniazid toxicity by enhancing its metabolism to hepatotoxic metabolites. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 36. Istradefylline: Rifampin decreases istradefylline levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Ivabradine: Rifampin reduces ivabradine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Ivacaftor: Rifampin decreases ivacaftor levels significantly (~9-fold) via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 39. Ivosidenib: Rifampin reduces ivosidenib levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Ixabepilone: Rifampin decreases ixabepilone levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 41. Ixazomib: Rifampin reduces ixazomib levels significantly (Cmax by 54%, AUC by 74%) via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 42. Lansoprazole: Rifampin decreases lansoprazole levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Lapatinib: Rifampin reduces lapatinib levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 44. Larotrectinib: Rifampin decreases larotrectinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. If co-administration is unavoidable, double the larotrectinib dose and revert to the original dose after discontinuing rifampin. 45. Lasmiditan: Rifampin increases lasmiditan levels by affecting P-gp efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 46. Lefamulin: Rifampin reduces lefamulin levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid co-administration unless the benefit outweighs the risk. 47. Lemborexant: Rifampin decreases lemborexant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 48. Lenolisib: Rifampin reduces lenolisib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 49. Letermovir: Rifampin decreases letermovir levels by affecting P-gp efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Lomitapide: Rifampin reduces lomitapide levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 51. Lopinavir: Rifampin decreases lopinavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 52. Loratadine: Rifampin reduces loratadine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 53. Lovastatin: Rifampin decreases lovastatin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 54. Lumateperone: Rifampin reduces lumateperone levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 55. Lurbinectedin: Rifampin decreases lurbinectedin levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Macimorelin: Rifampin reduces macimorelin levels via CYP3A4 induction, potentially causing false-positive test results. Discontinue rifampin before testing. 57. Macitentan: Rifampin decreases macitentan levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 58. Maraviroc: Rifampin reduces maraviroc levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 59. Mavorixafor: Rifampin decreases mavorixafor levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 60. Mestranol: Rifampin reduces mestranol levels by increasing its metabolism, potentially causing contraceptive failure. Use non-hormonal contraceptives. 61. Methadone: Rifampin decreases methadone levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 62. Methylprednisolone: Rifampin reduces methylprednisolone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 63. Midazolam: Rifampin decreases midazolam levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 64. Midostaurin: Rifampin reduces midostaurin levels significantly, leading to reduced efficacy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 65. Naldemedine: Rifampin decreases naldemedine levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 66. Neratinib: Rifampin reduces neratinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 67. Netupitant/Palonosetron: Rifampin decreases netupitant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 68. Nevirapine: Rifampin reduces nevirapine levels through CYP3A4 induction. Co-administration is contraindicated. 69. Nicardipine: Rifampin decreases nicardipine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 70. Nilotinib: Rifampin reduces nilotinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 71. Nintedanib: Rifampin decreases nintedanib levels by affecting P-gp transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 72. Nirogacestat: Rifampin reduces nirogacestat levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 73. Nisoldipine: Rifampin decreases nisoldipine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 74. Norethindrone: Rifampin reduces norethindrone levels, potentially causing contraceptive failure. Use non-hormonal contraceptives. 75. Norgestrel: Rifampin decreases norgestrel levels, increasing the risk of contraceptive failure. Use alternative or backup contraception. 76. Olanzapine/Samidorphan: Rifampin reduces olanzapine and samidorphan levels significantly (~50% and ~75%, respectively). Avoid or use an alternative drug. 77. Olaparib: Rifampin decreases olaparib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 78. Olutasidenib: Rifampin reduces olutasidenib levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 79. Omaveloxolone: Rifampin decreases omaveloxolone levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 80. Omeprazole: Rifampin reduces omeprazole levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 81. Osimertinib: Rifampin decreases osimertinib levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 82. Ozanimod: Rifampin reduces ozanimod levels by affecting CYP2C8 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 83. Palbociclib: Rifampin decreases palbociclib levels significantly (~85%) via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 84. Palovarotene: Rifampin reduces palovarotene levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 85. Pazopanib: Rifampin decreases pazopanib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 86. Pemigatinib: Rifampin reduces pemigatinib levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 87. Perampanel: Rifampin decreases perampanel levels via CYP3A4 induction. Increased perampanel doses may be required. 88. Pexidartinib: Rifampin alters pexidartinib levels, increasing hepatotoxicity risk. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 89. Pirtobrutinib: Rifampin reduces pirtobrutinib levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 90. Pretomanid: Rifampin decreases pretomanid levels and increases hepatotoxicity risk. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 91. Primaquine: Rifampin reduces primaquine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 92. Progesterone (all forms): Rifampin decreases progesterone levels, reducing contraceptive efficacy. Use non-hormonal contraceptives. 93. Propofol: Rifampin reduces propofol levels by inducing CYP2B6 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 94. Pyrazinamide: Rifampin increases pyrazinamide toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 95. Quazepam: Rifampin reduces quazepam levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 96. Quetiapine: Rifampin decreases quetiapine levels through CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 97. Quinidine: Rifampin reduces quinidine levels via CYP3A4 induction. Avoid or use an alternative drug. This list highlights the importance of monitoring and adjusting drug regimens when rifampin is co-administered, as it significantly impacts the metabolism and efficacy of numerous medications.
